speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in respect of recent studies which show that children having drug-abusing parents are more likely to take drugs later in life (a) what is the current number of generational-correlated drug offenders in Singapore; and (b) whether there are measures put in place to prevent the generational cycles of addiction.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But we recognise that the latter is a real risk.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: To address this, measures have been put in place to support families and children of offenders and ex-offenders.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Singapore Prison Service works with community partners to provide them social support.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Partners, such as Focus on the Family, The Salvation Army and Singapore Children Society. run family-bonding programmes within prisons.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: These programmes equip inmates with the relevant knowledge and skills to improve their relationship with their families and children during incarceration.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Member agencies in the Community Action for Rehabilitation of Ex-Offenders (CARE) Network, run programmes, such as the Yellow Ribbon Fund’s Yellow Brick Road and the Industrial and Services Co-operative Society Ltd (ISCOS) Fairy Godparent programmes.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: These programmes provide tuition support to improve the children's academic performance, befriending and mentorship programmes to develop the children’s socio-emotional competencies, and parenting skills workshop to improve the caregivers' parenting abilities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Under YEP, officers from the Singapore Police Force (SPF) and Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) also serve as mentors and conduct crime and drug prevention talks.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: CNB works with the Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs), polytechnics and universities to establish youth advocacy against drug use.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: CNB also works with the National Council Against Drug Abuse (NCADA) to raise awareness of the harms of drugs among youths.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: NCADA has established the United Against Drugs Coalition.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is a coalition of corporate and community establishments, such as clothing and food and beverage (F&B) companies popular among youths.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: NCADA engages these establishments to propagate the anti-drug message to their young customers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is also working closely with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and other Government agencies and community partners in an integrated approach to support at-risk children and youths, offenders and their families.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Committee facilitates collaborative efforts in research and data sharing, helps develop the capacity of organisations to support rehabilitation and coordinates efforts to address issues of offending and re-offending.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, tackling generational cycles of addiction requires many helping hands.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can we leverage their extended families or the community, such as school counsellors or the many community befrienders that we have, to strengthen the current efforts?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Second, can the Ministry also consider assigning a dedicated case manager to each of these at-risk children when their parents are arrested, so that proper support and care can be provided to them at an early stage?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: There have been many of such efforts ongoing, actually.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As I mentioned about the CARE Network, this network has worked in partnership with grassroots volunteers, family service centres and other voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs), and have been providing support to children of inmates and ex-offenders.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I also mentioned about the family bonding programmes run by the various community partners, such as the Salvation Army and Singapore Children's Society, which are targeted at inmates, children and caregivers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have also launched recently in July 2016 a CARE Network Children Support Programme.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Nevertheless, the thrust of the suggestion for us to do more and better has been well-noted and this is what the NCPR Committee will be reviewing and discussing, to see how we can intensify efforts to ensure that we can prevent intergenerational offending.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am aware that they have very young children at home.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We certainly agree with the need for more help to be given to children of ex-offenders, in particular, the sad situation when both parents are incarcerated.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, we have to do our best in an imperfect situation because we recognise that parents play a very big role in the lives of children.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Given this imperfect situation, relatives would have to come in, the community would have to rally and help to fill in the gaps.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: One of the key areas we are training them is to give them the skills and support to ensure that they can play a role in rekindling familiar bonds, providing positive pro-social support and better identifying vulnerable children.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And as I mentioned, one of the roles of NCPR is also to see what else can be done.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We recognise their gaps and it is something that we got to make the best of in an imperfect situation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned just now that we are currently not collecting data on the generational-correlated offenders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I am just wondering whether MHA can start collecting such data, so that all the programmes that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned, we can see whether it is working, and we can start to see whether the trend is going up or going down as well.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But it is quite a challenge because some of these families, there has been a breakdown in family relationships.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: For some of them, they have not been in touch with their spouses and may not know where their children are.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We have a rough sense, but we are not able to share because there needs to be more work put in into this.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Yes, definitely, we would be very keen to help.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: But from my last 12 years as an advisor, I never get any information on this.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, I am just thinking, maybe the first cut of help should come from those who know about the case – the agency which comes in to help.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And then, if you think that the community or the advisor can help, then refer those cases to us.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Because you would know who the repeat offenders are.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: When they go in, you can check the background and then can also check whether they have young children at home.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, we have got quite a number of volunteers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, I will certainly check whether the Member's constituency is involved, and we will link the Member up with the right resources to ensure that the Member's residents will get the support they need.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Ideally, family should be the rightful caregivers for children, but we know that our society is not ideal and there are some dysfunctional families where the children may be better off if they are housed in a boarding school, say, on weekdays, and they go back on weekends.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But for now, we would look at family as the first line of defence, in particular.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Even when their parents are incarcerated, there are others like grandparents, aunts and uncles, who can help.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We would actually look to family as the first line of defence.
